## Extraction report — 1705.02768v1 (Sumi–Miyazaki–Sakata, "Typical ranks of semi-tall real 3-tensors")

**Counts.** 75 nodes, 65 edges. By type: 21 definition, 11 claim, 10 lemma, 6 proof (18 proof_step children), 3 remark, 2 corollary, 2 theorem, 1 example, 1 open_problem. 31 nodes came from `latex_facts` environments, 26 from prose (definitions/claims/open problem/2 unwrapped proofs hiding between environments), 18 are proof_steps. Edges: 58 uses, 6 proves, 1 resolves (the paper's own open problem → its main theorem, `OpenP1.1 →resolves→ TP1.1`).

**Steps per parent:** PP1.1 (Lemma 3.6 proof): 3 top-level (6 incl. nested) · PP1.2 (Lemma 4.5 proof): 5 · PP1.3 (main-theorem proof): 0 — 2-sentence body, no part/step labels · PP1.4 (prose proof of the key lemma, hiding between F18 and F20 in the facts): 0 — 1-sentence body · PP1.5 (prose proof of Lemma 5.3): 4 · PP1.6 (prose proof of Lemma 5.4): 3.

**Coverage.** statement_short: 100% of proofs (6/6), 100% of steps (18/18), 11/57 Level‑1 nodes overall (concentrated on proofs/algorithms-equivalent and notation-dense lemmas, per spec). Mean node confidence 0.87 (75/75 have it, incl. steps — the spec's per-type field lists omit confidence/section/origin for steps but the confidence rule says "every node," so I filled them to be safe; flagging as a spec ambiguity). Mean edge confidence 0.86. `rigor_nonformal_count: 3` (two "easily verified"/terse-derivation claims in §4, one "by counting the dimensions" bound in §1). 10 nodes `origin: external` (Chevalley, Catalisano–Geramita–Gimigliano, ten Berge, Harris, and four citations to the authors' own prior papers sms13/15/17).

**Orphans:** 1 — `DP1.18` (the $T_k$/$PTQ$ slice notation in §2) is never referenced by name again; the GL-invariance it states underlies later reduction arguments only implicitly.

**finalize() report:** 0 errors, 0 warnings. 12 labels filled, 10 `\ref`-stated `uses` edges auto-added, 0 flagged `backward`, 0 unresolved refs, 17-entry label table written to `metadata.labels`.

**Spec ambiguities/gaps hit, reported honestly:**
1. Two implicit, unwrapped proofs exist in the source — the proof of the "key lemma" (4.2) and part of the proof of Lemma 5.3 — where the paper never writes `\begin{proof}`, just runs the derivation in prose between two environments. `latex_facts.py` can't see these (environments only), so I promoted them to `proof` nodes myself (PP1.4, PP1.5 share territory with PP1.6) and added their `proves` edges manually. This is squarely "your main job" per the spec's two-layers section, but it's worth flagging since it means proof *nodes*, not just definitions/claims, can be hiding in prose.
2. Several short lead-in sentences ("Then by Lemma `\ref{lem:key}`, Fact `\ref{fac:deg}` and Bezout's theorem, we see the following") contain real `\ref`s to other nodes but aren't part of any node's own statement, so the pipeline's automatic `\ref`→`uses` pass never sees them. I added these as manual edges (e.g. `LP1.3/ClP1.2 → CP1.1`), but this is a structural gap between the "facts only cover environments" design and this paper's referencing style.
3. A couple of external claims ("the r-th higher secant variety... is the whole space," classical but uncited by `\cite`) had no explicit citation macro at all — I still marked them `origin: external` per the content rule, with a best-effort `origin_citation`, flagged with lower confidence (0.6) since the attribution is my judgment call, not the text's.
4. `resolves` edges are typed `problem/open_problem/conjecture → theorem-like/algorithm`, which fit the one open problem in this paper cleanly, but the paper itself frames that open problem only in connective prose ("...is still left open"), never as a labeled environment — same promotion pattern as above.

All `statement` fields are verbatim copies of source spans (environment or prose), slice-verified against `facts.json`'s cleaned `source` text before being written — no paraphrasing applied to `statement`. `statement_short`, where populated, is my own compression.
